questions.stem: Rabindranath Tagore was awarded the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature primarily for which English-translated work?

options.option_text: Gora — a novel exploring Hindu identity and nationalism
Gitanjali — a collection of lyric devotional poetry
The Home and the World — a novel about the Swadeshi movement
Manasi — his celebrated collection of Bengali romantic verse

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Nobel citation specifically praised Gitanjali (Song Offerings), the English-translated verse collection Tagore sent to W.B. Yeats, for its 'profoundly sensitive, fresh and beautiful verse.' Manasi (A) is a distractor because it is an important early poetry collection but was never translated for the Nobel committee. Gora and The Home and the World are celebrated novels but were not the basis of the prize.

questions.stem: The Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences differs from the five original Nobel Prizes in one fundamental respect. What is it?

options.option_text: It carries a larger cash award than the other five Nobel categories
It was established in 1968 by Sveriges Riksbank, not Alfred Nobel's will
It is awarded by the Norwegian Nobel Committee based in Oslo, Norway
Its winners must be affiliated with a recognised university or institution

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Economics prize (full name: Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel) was created in 1968 by Sweden's central bank to mark its 300th anniversary — it does not appear in Nobel's 1895 will. Option C is wrong: Oslo hosts only the Peace Prize; the Economics prize is awarded in Stockholm by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, exactly like Physics and Chemistry.

questions.stem: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar won the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics for the theoretical concept known as the 'Chandrasekhar Limit.' This limit specifies the?

options.option_text: Minimum mass required for a nebula to collapse into a protostar
Maximum mass of a white dwarf star beyond which it collapses further
Threshold temperature at which stellar hydrogen fusion becomes self-sustaining
Maximum radius a red giant can attain before shedding its outer envelope

questions.explanation: B is correct: Chandrasekhar proved that a white dwarf with mass above ~1.4 solar masses cannot remain stable and must collapse into a neutron star or black hole. This limit (~1.4 M☉) is fundamental to understanding stellar evolution and supernovae. Option C (fusion threshold) describes the ignition condition for main-sequence stars, a separate concept entirely. Chandrasekhar was Indian-American, born in Lahore.

questions.stem: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, not Stockholm, as specified in Alfred Nobel's own will. Which body is mandated to select the Peace Prize laureate each year?

options.option_text: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm, Sweden
The United Nations Security Council based in New York, USA
The Norwegian Nobel Committee appointed by the Storting (Parliament)
The International Committee of the Red Cross based in Geneva, Switzerland

questions.explanation: C is correct: Nobel's will explicitly named a committee of five persons chosen by the Norwegian Parliament (Storting) to award the Peace Prize. This explains why Peace is the only prize given in Oslo. The Royal Swedish Academy (A) handles Physics, Chemistry and Economics. The ICRC (D) has itself won the Peace Prize three times but does not award it. The UN has no role in Nobel selections.

questions.stem: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) jointly received the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize 'for their efforts to build up and disseminate greater knowledge about man-made climate change.' Who was the individual co-recipient?

options.option_text: Wangari Maathai — Kenyan environmental activist and tree-planting pioneer
Al Gore — former US Vice President and climate change campaigner
Kofi Annan — former UN Secretary-General and global peace diplomat
Ban Ki-moon — UN Secretary-General who championed global climate summits

questions.explanation: B is correct: Al Gore shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with the IPCC for his documentary 'An Inconvenient Truth' and widespread public awareness campaign on climate change. Wangari Maathai (A) is a common distractor — she won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2004 (not 2007) for her Green Belt Movement. Kofi Annan won in 2001 (jointly with the UN itself). Ban Ki-moon never received the Nobel Peace Prize.

questions.stem: Which Nobel Prize in Literature laureate was compelled to DECLINE the award in 1958 under Soviet pressure, though his son later accepted the medal and diploma posthumously on his behalf in 1989?

options.option_text: Mikhail Sholokhov — Soviet author of And Quiet Flows the Don
Alexander Solzhenitsyn — author of The Gulag Archipelago (Nobel 1970)
Boris Pasternak — Russian author of Doctor Zhivago (Nobel 1958)
Bertolt Brecht — German Marxist playwright and poet of the 20th century

questions.explanation: C is correct: Boris Pasternak initially accepted the 1958 Nobel Prize in Literature for Doctor Zhivago, but Khrushchev's regime threatened him with exile; he then sent a telegram declining the prize. The Soviet Writers' Union expelled him. His son Yevgeny accepted the medal and diploma in 1989 during Gorbachev's glasnost era. Solzhenitsyn (B) is the most tempting distractor — he did face Soviet hostility over his 1970 Nobel, but he did not formally decline; he accepted it in absentia and collected it in person in 1974 after his expulsion.

questions.stem: The 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was jointly awarded for determining the atomic structure and function of the ribosome. Which Indian-origin scientist was among the three co-recipients?

options.option_text: Har Gobind Khorana — who deciphered the genetic code (Nobel 1968)
Venkatraman Ramakrishnan — British-American structural biologist
Ahmed Zewail — Egyptian-American pioneer of femtochemistry (Nobel 1999)
K. Barry Sharpless — American chemist specialising in click chemistry

questions.explanation: B is correct: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan (born in Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu) shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Thomas Steitz and Ada Yonath for X-ray crystallographic studies of the 30S ribosomal subunit. He was working at the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, Cambridge. Har Gobind Khorana (A) is the most tempting distractor as another Indian-origin Nobel laureate in a biological science — but he won the 1968 Nobel in Physiology or Medicine, not Chemistry, and for cracking the genetic code, not ribosome structure.
